claim: Kim et al. use attack success probability (ASP) as an attacker-side effectiveness metric
quote: The attack success probability (𝐴𝑆𝑃 ) can be computed by the Eq. 2:

claim: Kim row, property 1 (campaign persistence): has it in part
quote: The automated attack consists of four stages of the CKC and its objective is to compromise a vulnerability (i.e., CVE 2021–41773) of an Apache web server [87].
locator: Sec. 5.2, p. 7 printed (PDF p. 7); attacks as independent Poisson arrivals, Sec. 6.1 p. 9
issue: Multi-stage toward one objective (behaviour yes), each attack a fresh Poisson-arrival run (qualifier no): partial follows the dissertation's rule.

claim: Kim row, property 5 (detection avoidance): has it in part, because the evasion is assumed
quote: After the attacker succeeds to connect to a victim, it assumes that creating an outbound connection is attempted in order to evade the detection by a defense system such as a network intrusion detection system (NIDS) or a firewall.
issue: Kim's own 'it assumes' carries the 'assumed' cell of Table C.1.

quote: Our proposed attack model is assumed to follow some steps. The attacker first attempts to find an IP address of a target in a network and then collects information on the target's web services.
issue: One fixed sequence toward one objective (a shell); no choice, response to MTD, cost weighing or memory is described anywhere in the paper.

claim: Kim row, property 8 (deployment-strategy awareness): has none
quote: At each CKC phase (𝑘), attackers can determine the remaining available time (𝑇𝑘) after successfully completing the preceding step.
locator: Sec. 6.1, p. 10 printed (PDF p. 10); all MTD techniques triggered 'at the same time', Sec. 5.3, p. 8
issue: Kim's words make 'predicts ... when' true of the attacker (and U0290 says so). The none mark holds only because Table C.1 keeps row 8's 'predicts and leverages' as one predicate, while row 5 is split at its 'and'; split the same way, Kim would score in part. The mark is defensible but rests on an asymmetric predicate split an examiner may question.
fix_text: either split row 8 at 'and' as row 5 is (Kim -> in part) or state in App. C why row 8 is one predicate

claim: Kim row in Table 6.1 (copy of Table 3.3 row): 1 in part, 5 in part, rest none
quote: At each CKC phase (𝑘), attackers can determine the remaining available time (𝑇𝑘) after successfully completing the preceding step.
issue: Identical to U0263: marks 1, 5 and the five crosses are supported; the property-8 cross depends on row 8 not being split at 'and' (see U0263).

claim: Kim's reverse shell is chosen 'in order to evade the detection by a defense system' (p. 7)
quote: After the attacker succeeds to connect to a victim, it assumes that creating an outbound connection is attempted in order to evade the detection by a defense system such as a network intrusion detection system (NIDS) or a firewall.
locator: Sec. 5.2, p. 7 printed (PDF p. 7); pinpoint correct
issue: Quote verbatim; 'reverse shell' is the dissertation's name for Kim's 'outbound connection' (Kim uses 'reverse connections' in Sec. 5.1).

claim: Kim's testbed runs no IDS, so the evasion is assumed
quote: A No-MTD system is considered as a baseline of the measurements that operate to handle network packets without any defense mechanisms.
issue: Kim never states that no IDS runs; the claim is inferred from the IDS's absence from the testbed description (Fig. 4, Sec. 6.1) and the defence-free baseline. 'it assumes' (p. 7) does support 'the evasion is assumed'.
fix_text: 'but the testbed runs no IDS' -> 'but the paper describes no IDS in the testbed'

claim: Kim's attacker 'can determine the remaining available time' before the next MTD deployment (p. 10)
quote: At each CKC phase (𝑘), attackers can determine the remaining available time (𝑇𝑘) after successfully completing the preceding step.
locator: Sec. 6.1, Eq. 2-3, p. 10 printed (PDF p. 10); pinpoint correct
issue: Verbatim, but T_k is a term of Kim's ASP formula (Eq. 2), i.e. the evaluators' quantity; nothing in the attack script computes it.

claim: Every mechanism deploys at once, so the attacker predicts which mechanism deploys next and when, but no technique leverages it
quote: we first design and develop a naive configuration that triggers the operations of all MTD techniques at the same time on a regular basis.
issue: 'every mechanism deploys at once' is supported (though server resources reset on a separate T_RST = 2 x T_MTD). 'it predicts which mechanism deploys next' is the dissertation's inference: Kim says only that attackers can determine remaining time, inside an ASP formula. 'so it predicts' reads the formula as attacker behaviour.
fix_text: 'so it predicts which mechanism deploys next and when' -> 'so in Kim's ASP formula it knows when the next deployment comes'
